audience: smart beginner, comfortable with dice + lists
core_claim: Convolution mixes two lists by flipped sliding dot-products; dice sums are the canonical example

key_concepts.definition_1line: New list where out[n] = sum_k a[k] b[n-k]
key_concepts.name: Discrete convolution
key_concepts.why_matters: Gives sum-of-dice distribution, polynomial product, image blur

key_concepts.definition_1line: 36 pairs; constant-sum pairs lie on diagonals
key_concepts.name: Dice pair grid

key_concepts.definition_1line: Bars of P(X=n) with DecimalNumber labels
key_concepts.name: Distribution bars
key_concepts.why_matters: From counting to weighted probabilities a_i, b_j

mechanism_steps: List 36 die pairs in grid; diagonals = constant sum
Flip second row so sum-7 aligns vertically
Slide offset; aligned column = pairs for that sum
Uniform: count; weighted: multiply a_i b_j then add
narration_beats_3b1b_style: Hook: quiz adding two normals, then warmup dice
Intuition: grid diagonals + flipped sliding rows
Formalize: convolution term late, table-diagonal dual view
